summary: 302.ai, a Hong Kong-based AI aggregator operated by Univerads Technology Limited, left a Microsoft Azure storage bucket publicly accessible without authentication or encryption. Cybernews researchers found it on August 2, 2026: 17.6 million files (22.72 TB), including over 144,000 user chat logs with prompts, AI responses and personal details (birth dates, genders, addresses, contact information), plus enterprise customers' corporate documents and chatbot logs. Researchers notified the company on August 11 and the bucket was closed by September 8, 2026.
